## Side and back material in Windows 0.24.28

3D Studio uses the front reference to guide the finish on the two sides and the back of a generated sculpture. It samples an interior patch on the lower portion of the subject and projects the pattern around the surface. All three cameras sample the same locations on the model, including where the camera views meet. The image renderer refines those views locally. The final GLB embeds their textures alongside the original front photograph.

The transfer depends on the visible material. Strong painted markings can carry across the body, while softer references contribute fine grain. Material color differences reduce the transfer on mixed surfaces. A front reference without a usable sample uses the existing angle renderer. The sides and back are inferred from the available reference.

## Side and back material, Windows 0.24.28

Repainted the 0.24.27 owl and compared both GLBs in the Workbench viewer at four fixed angles. The mesh retained all 99,163 triangles with identical coordinates and winding. Vertex normals agreed within 0.00001, and the front photo and its per-triangle UV coordinates matched. The back and wings gained visible cobalt feather markings. A second test used the bundled red panda and walnut moon. The first sample transferred a tail stripe to the wood. After limiting low-contrast transfer to grain, the broad stripe disappeared.

Measured the mean absolute difference between 2-pixel and 13-pixel Gaussian blurs on the overlapping interiors of the old and new texture atlases (8-bit RGB). Left changed from 5.68 to 14.82, back from 3.49 to 16.17, and right from 10.12 to 18.35. Also checked a uniform reference, a fully transparent reference, and texture continuity across the rear meridian.

A fresh Windows Create run on an RTX 3060 completed in 143.3 seconds and saved a 4,484,356-byte model with 100,059 triangles and four embedded textures. The reference-pattern path was active. Verified export fingerprint, orbit, navigation during creation, and reopening the saved model.
